subject: DI04005021

body.en:
Definition / principle

Mass transfer is the transport of a species relative to a mixture or across a phase boundary under a suitable driving force. A mass-transfer operation uses such transport to separate or recover components.

Detailed theory and conditions

Separation requires both a thermodynamic possibility and a sufficiently rapid rate. Equilibrium limits the attainable separation; diffusion, contact area and contact time influence the rate. Examples include absorbing a gas into a liquid, extracting a solute between two liquids and dissolving soluble material from a solid. A heat exchanger transferring energy is not automatically a mass-transfer separator; pure bulk transport of an unchanged mixture is not selective separation. Material balances establish quantities, while equilibrium and rate information establish achievable compositions and equipment needs.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

યોગ્ય driving force હેઠળ mixture માં species નો relative transport અથવા phase boundary પાર transport એટલે Mass transfer. Components ને separate/recover કરવા આ transport વાપરતી process એટલે mass-transfer operation.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Separation માટે thermodynamic possibility તથા પૂરતો transfer rate બંને જોઈએ. Equilibrium attainable separation limit કરે છે; diffusion, contact area તથા time rate નક્કી કરે છે. Gas absorption, liquid extraction તથા solid માંથી soluble material dissolve કરવું examples છે. F ક્ત heat exchanger માં energy transfer અથવા unchanged mixture નું bulk transport selective mass separation નથી. Material balance quantities આપે છે; equilibrium તથા rate attainable compositions/equipment નક્કી કરે છે.

body.en:
Definition

Phase-based classification identifies the phases participating in selective component transfer; the operation name also depends on the separating mechanism.

Gas–liquid

Absorption transfers a soluble gas into liquid; stripping transfers a volatile dissolved component from liquid into gas. Distillation uses vapor–liquid equilibrium and energy to redistribute volatile components.

Liquid–liquid

Extraction distributes a solute between two liquid phases that are not completely mutually miscible. The solvent must create a useful selectivity and separable phases.

Solid–liquid and solid–fluid

Leaching dissolves soluble material from a solid using liquid solvent. Adsorption accumulates a component on a solid surface from gas or liquid; it is not bulk absorption. Drying includes transfer of moisture from a wet material to a gas; crystallization forms a solid from a supersaturated liquid.

Qualification

Membrane operations are classified additionally by the selective barrier and driving force; they do not require direct mixing of the two bulk streams. This classification introduces related operations without adding their design derivations to this syllabus.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Selective component transfer માં ભાગ લેતી phases મુજબ classification થાય છે. Operation નું નામ separation mechanism પર પણ આધારિત છે.

Gas–liquid

Absorption માં soluble gas liquid માં જાય છે; stripping માં dissolved volatile component liquid માંથી gas માં જાય છે. Distillation માં vapor–liquid equilibrium તથા energy વડે volatile components redistribute થાય છે.

Liquid–liquid

સંપૂર્ણ mutually miscible ન હોય તેવી બે liquid phases વચ્ચે solute distribution એટલે extraction. Solvent થી ઉપયોગી selectivity તથા separable phases મળવા જોઈએ.

Solid–liquid તથા Solid–fluid

Leaching માં liquid solvent વડે solid માંનું soluble material dissolve થાય છે. Adsorption માં gas/liquid નો component solid surface પર accumulate થાય છે; તે bulk absorption નથી. Drying માં wet material નું moisture gas માં જાય છે; crystallization માં supersaturated liquid માંથી solid બને છે.

નોંધ

Membrane operations માટે selective barrier તથા driving force મુજબ વધારાનું classification થાય છે; bulk streams ને directly mix કરવી જરૂરી નથી. Related operations નો અહીં પરિચય છે; syllabus બહારની design derivations ઉમેરાતી નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Membrane separation uses a selective barrier to preferentially transmit components and retain others; the products are permeate and retentate.

Detailed theory and conditions

A module has a feed side, a selective membrane and a permeate side. Selectivity may arise from pore size or from sorption/diffusion through a dense membrane. Pressure-driven microfiltration/ultrafiltration remove particles or macromolecules; reverse osmosis mainly removes dissolved salts using pressure exceeding the effective osmotic opposition. Gas separation uses permeability/selectivity and a partial-pressure difference; dialysis uses a chemical-potential/concentration driving force, while electrodialysis uses an electric field and ion-selective membranes. Applications include water treatment, protein concentration and gas purification. Fouling, concentration polarization, membrane compatibility, pretreatment, cleaning and energy requirements limit performance. A membrane does not give perfect separation simply because it has small pores.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Selective barrier કેટલાક components ને preferentially pass કરીને બીજાં retain કરે તે membrane separation છે. Products permeate તથા retentate છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Module માં feed side, selective membrane તથા permeate side હોય છે. Selectivity pore size અથવા dense membrane માં sorption/diffusion થી મળી શકે છે. Pressure-driven microfiltration/ultrafiltration particles/macromolecules દૂર કરે છે. RO માં effective osmotic opposition કરતાં વધુ pressure થી dissolved salts મુખ્યત્વે દૂર થાય છે. Gas separation permeability/selectivity તથા partial-pressure difference વાપરે છે. Dialysis concentration/chemical-potential અને electrodialysis electric field તથા ion-selective membrane વાપરે છે. Water treatment, protein concentration તથા gas purification ઉપયોગો છે. Fouling, concentration polarization, compatibility, pretreatment, cleaning તથા energy performance limit કરે છે. નાના pores એટલે હંમેશાં perfect separation નહીં.

body.en:
Definition / principle

In this classification, direct operations generate the separating phases from the original solution by adding or removing heat. Indirect operations add a foreign separating substance.

Detailed theory and conditions

Classification first: direct examples include fractional distillation and fractional crystallization driven by heat addition/removal. Indirect examples include absorption, stripping, liquid extraction, leaching and adsorption using an added solvent, gas or solid agent. Direct methods avoid a deliberately added separating material, but may require substantial energy. Indirect methods can give a useful selectivity when direct separation is impractical, but solvent/agent recovery, losses, product contamination and materials compatibility can add cost. If the required product is already a solution, the agent need not always be removed. Do not confuse this terminology with physical direct contact: a packed absorber is a direct-contact device but an indirect operation in this textbook classification.[1]

Reference: [1] Treybal, The Mass-Transfer Operations, Chapter1.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

આ classification માં heat ઉમેરવા/દૂર કરવાથી original solution માં separating phases ઉત્પન્ન થાય તે direct operation છે. Foreign separating substance ઉમેરાય તે indirect operation છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Classification: heat addition/removal થી fractional distillation તથા crystallization direct examples છે. Added solvent/gas/solid agent વાપરતાં absorption, stripping, liquid extraction, leaching તથા adsorption indirect examples છે. Direct methods માં foreign separating material ઉમેરાતું નથી, પણ energy વધુ લાગી શકે છે. Indirect methods ઉપયોગી selectivity આપે છે, પરંતુ agent recovery/loss, contamination તથા compatibility cost વધારી શકે છે. Product solution જ required હોય તો agent હંમેશાં દૂર કરવો જરૂરી નથી. Physical direct contact થી આ terminology જુદી છે. Packed absorber direct-contact device છે પણ textbook classification માં indirect operation છે.[1]

Reference: [1] Treybal, The Mass-Transfer Operations, Chapter1.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Choosing a separation method means selecting a feasible operation and separating agent to meet purity, recovery, capacity and safety targets economically.

Detailed theory and conditions

First identify feed phase, composition, flow and target products. Check usable property differences: volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size or membrane permeability. Examine equilibrium selectivity and the obtainable driving force, then rate/contact area and energy or solvent requirements. Include solvent recovery, product contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment and control flexibility. A cheap solvent may be expensive overall if it is difficult to regenerate. A single operation may not meet both high recovery and purity, so an integrated sequence may be preferable without assuming that every separation needs distillation.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Purity, recovery, capacity તથા safety targets economical રીતે મેળવવા feasible operation તથા separating agent પસંદ કરવાં એટલે separation-method selection.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

પહેલાં feed phase, composition, flow તથા target products ઓળખો. Volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size અથવા membrane permeability નો ઉપયોગી difference શોધો. Equilibrium selectivity/driving force પછી rate, area તથા energy/solvent જરૂરિયાત જુઓ. Solvent recovery, contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment તથા control flexibility ગણો. Regeneration મુશ્કેલ હોય તો સસ્તો solvent overall મોંઘો પડી શકે છે. High purity તથા recovery માટે integrated sequence જરૂરી થઈ શકે; દરેક separation માટે distillation જ જરૂરી નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Solute recovery preferentially removes a desired or unwanted component. Fractionation splits a mixture into fractions of differing compositions. Unsteady operation changes inventory/composition with time; steady operation has no time accumulation in the selected control volume.

Detailed theory and conditions

A batch vessel can be perfectly mixed yet unsteady because solute concentration changes during contact. A continuous plant can be unsteady during start-up, upsets or shutdown. At steady state, inlets and outlets balance without accumulation, although composition can change along the equipment. Solute recovery and fractionation describe separation purpose; batch and continuous describe operation. They are independent classifications rather than mutually exclusive names for the same choice.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Solute recovery માં desired/unwanted component preferentially દૂર થાય છે. Fractionation માં mixture જુદી compositions ના fractions માં વહેંચાય છે. Unsteady operation માં time સાથે inventory/composition બદલાય છે. Steady operation ના control volume માં time accumulation નથી.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Perfectly mixed batch vessel પણ contact દરમિયાન composition બદલાતી હોવાથી unsteady હોય છે. Continuous plant start-up/upset/shutdown વખતે unsteady હોઈ શકે છે. Steady state પર accumulation નથી, પરંતુ equipment ની length પ્રમાણે composition બદલાઈ શકે છે. Recovery/fractionation separation purpose છે; batch/continuous operation mode છે. આ independent classifications છે, એક જ choice ના alternate names નથી.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Definition / principle

A stagewise operation uses identifiable contacting/separation steps. A continuous-contact operation allows interfacial exchange progressively along the contacting region without imposed equilibrium stages.

Detailed theory and conditions

An ideal stage leaves its exiting phases at equilibrium; an actual stage normally falls short and needs an efficiency definition. Mixer–settlers and tray columns are stagewise contactors. Packed towers provide differential continuous contact, but their plant flow can still be steady. Tray towers may also process continuous gas/liquid flows: continuous throughput does not convert their contacting into differential contact. A cascade connects stages co-currently, countercurrently or crosscurrently; the chosen arrangement changes local driving forces and solvent usage.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Stagewise operation માં ઓળખી શકાય તેવા contacting/separation steps હોય છે. Continuous-contact operation માં imposed equilibrium stages વગર contacting region દરમિયાન સતત interfacial exchange થાય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Ideal stage ના departing phases equilibrium માં હોય છે. Actual stage માટે efficiency જરૂરી છે. Mixer–settlers તથા tray columns stagewise છે. Packed tower differential continuous contact આપે છે અને plant flow steady હોઈ શકે છે. Tray tower માં પણ continuous gas/liquid throughput હોય છે; તેના કારણે contacting differential બનતું નથી. Cascades co-current, countercurrent અથવા crosscurrent હોઈ શકે છે. Arrangement driving force તથા solvent usage બદલે છે.

Volatility, solubility, distribution, particle size અથવા membrane permeability નો ઉપયોગી difference શોધો. Equilibrium selectivity/driving force પછી rate, area તથા energy/solvent જરૂરિયાત જુઓ. Solvent recovery, contamination, thermal sensitivity, corrosion, toxicity, flammability, waste treatment તથા control flexibility ગણો. Regeneration મુશ્કેલ હોય તો સસ્તો solvent overall મોંઘો પડી શકે છે. High purity તથા recovery માટે integrated sequence જરૂરી થઈ શકે; દરેક separation માટે distillation જ જરૂરી નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Recovery,fractionation,batch and steady operation.
q.gu: Recovery,Fractionation,Batch તથા Steady Operation ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Solute recovery preferentially removes a desired or unwanted component. Fractionation splits a mixture into fractions of differing compositions. Unsteady operation changes inventory/composition with time; steady operation has no time accumulation in the selected control volume. A batch vessel can be perfectly mixed yet unsteady because solute concentration changes during contact. A continuous plant can be unsteady during start-up, upsets or shutdown. At steady state, inlets and outlets balance without accumulation, although composition can change along the equipment. Solute recovery and fractionation describe separation purpose; batch and continuous describe operation. They are independent classifications rather than mutually exclusive names for the same choice.
a.gu: Solute recovery માં desired/unwanted component preferentially દૂર થાય છે. Fractionation માં mixture જુદી compositions ના fractions માં વહેંચાય છે. Unsteady operation માં time સાથે inventory/composition બદલાય છે. Steady operation ના control volume માં time accumulation નથી. Perfectly mixed batch vessel પણ contact દરમિયાન composition બદલાતી હોવાથી unsteady હોય છે. Continuous plant start-up/upset/shutdown વખતે unsteady હોઈ શકે છે. Steady state પર accumulation નથી, પરંતુ equipment ની length પ્રમાણે composition બદલાઈ શકે છે. Recovery/fractionation separation purpose છે; batch/continuous operation mode છે. આ independent classifications છે, એક જ choice ના alternate names નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Stagewise and continuous-contact operations.
q.gu: Stagewise તથા Continuous-contact Operations ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A stagewise operation uses identifiable contacting/separation steps. A continuous-contact operation allows interfacial exchange progressively along the contacting region without imposed equilibrium stages. An ideal stage leaves its exiting phases at equilibrium; an actual stage normally falls short and needs an efficiency definition. Mixer–settlers and tray columns are stagewise contactors. Packed towers provide differential continuous contact, but their plant flow can still be steady. Tray towers may also process continuous gas/liquid flows: continuous throughput does not convert their contacting into differential contact. A cascade connects stages co-currently, countercurrently or crosscurrently; the chosen arrangement changes local driving forces and solvent usage.
a.gu: Stagewise operation માં ઓળખી શકાય તેવા contacting/separation steps હોય છે. Continuous-contact operation માં imposed equilibrium stages વગર contacting region દરમિયાન સતત interfacial exchange થાય છે. Ideal stage ના departing phases equilibrium માં હોય છે. Actual stage માટે efficiency જરૂરી છે. Mixer–settlers તથા tray columns stagewise છે. Packed tower differential continuous contact આપે છે અને plant flow steady હોઈ શકે છે. Tray tower માં પણ continuous gas/liquid throughput હોય છે; તેના કારણે contacting differential બનતું નથી. Cascades co-current, countercurrent અથવા crosscurrent હોઈ શકે છે. Arrangement driving force તથા solvent usage બદલે છે.
